variants.headline: {{master}} takes us as vassal
body: Our nation has entered vassalage under {{master}}. The course of our state now answers to another court.

variants.headline: An era of our own counsel, concluded
body: We answered to no court but our own, and gave our own counsel in war and peace. That independence is past: our nation has taken {{master}} as master, and our answers now pass through their court. What remains is a realm that remembers standing alone.

variants.headline: Who signed us into vassalage?
body: Citizens, our court has handed the nation to {{master}}. Ask who agreed to it, and what they got for giving us away. A people kept in the dark deserve the ledger of this bargain.

variants.headline: What vassalage under {{master}} means
body: Vassalage binds our foreign policy to {{master}}'s, and our wars may no longer be ours alone to choose. The tribute and the protection come as one package, and which side of it weighs more will show in the seasons ahead.

variants.headline: Our defensive pact with {{ally}} is at an end
body: The defensive pact between our nation and {{ally}} has come to an end. We are not at war with them, and the parting, so far as the record shows, is a matter of policy rather than battle.

variants.headline: A defensive pact comes to an end
body: One of our defensive pacts has come to an end. The other state has not gone to war with us, and the parting, so far as the record shows, is a matter of policy rather than battle.

variants.headline: The pact with {{ally}} is gone, and the guarantee with it
body: A defensive pact is a promise to fight together. Without it, an attack on {{ally}} no longer calls us to arms, and an attack on us calls no one. Our generals should read the map as it now stands, not as it stood last season.

variants.headline: Madam, must we lose every friend we have?
body: I read that the pact with {{ally}} has lapsed, and I recall what it cost to build. Wars begin in seasons when nobody wants them, and it is the treaties that hold until then. If the court will not renew it, let it at least say why.

variants.headline: We sign a defensive pact with {{ally}}
body: Our nation and {{ally}} have entered a defensive pact. From this day, an attack on either state is an attack on both.

variants.headline: A defensive pact is signed
body: Our nation has entered a defensive pact with a major power. From this day, an attack on either state is an attack on both.

variants.headline: Hear it! We stand with {{ally}}
body: People of the nation, take note. A defensive pact is signed with {{ally}}, and it holds from this day. Let any hand raised against us know what it answers to.

variants.headline: A pact for the palace, a question for the street
body: The court has promised our armies to {{ally}} if war comes looking. Perhaps that is wisdom, and perhaps it is our sons who will answer for it. The paper wants the terms read aloud in the square before anyone cheers.

variants.headline: Letters from the court: a pact with {{ally}}
body: We are informed that a defensive pact has lately been concluded between our nation and {{ally}}. The two peoples now stand together in war as in peace.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} denounces our nation
body: {{civilization}} has publicly denounced us. The declaration signals hostility between our two states, though it is not itself a declaration of war.

variants.headline: The square heard it first
body: A fishwife came back from the market with the news before any gazette had it: {{civilization}} has denounced us. By evening every stall had an opinion, and most of them were loud.

variants.headline: Let the denunciation be answered
body: {{civilization}} has called our nation out before the world. The paper's answer: count our walls, count our allies, and give no apology that is not owed. Firmness now costs less than regret later.

variants.headline: In this year, {{civilization}} spoke against us
body: In this season the court of {{civilization}} set down a denunciation against our nation, where none stood before. The record notes the fact and the season, and no more.

variants.headline: First contact with {{stranger}}
body: Our people have met {{stranger}} for the first time. The two nations now know each other, and the map has one fewer blank space.

variants.headline: They say strangers came over the hill
body: It is told that our scouts stood a long while on the ridge, watching fires that were not ours. By morning they had names for them: {{stranger}}. The walkers came home with the story, and the story has not stopped traveling since.

variants.headline: A new people, and new roads to walk
body: We are informed that our nation has opened relations with {{stranger}}. Every first meeting is a door: new trades, new maps, and one more seat at the table of nations.

variants.headline: We just met {{stranger}}
body: First contact confirmed. {{stranger}} is on the map now. More as we learn it.

variants.headline: {{first}} and {{second}} sign a defensive pact
body: Two foreign powers have bound their defenses together. {{first}} and {{second}} have signed a defensive pact, and an attack on either will now draw the other in.

variants.headline: Two foreign powers bind their defenses
body: A defensive pact has been signed between two foreign powers. Neither of them is ours, and an attack on either will now draw the other in.

variants.headline: The pact between {{first}} and {{second}} redraws the arithmetic
body: Two rivals have stopped quarreling and started planning together. If {{first}} and {{second}} hold to this pact, any war on our part must now plan for both at once. Alliances are cheap to sign and dear to test, but a prudent staff counts them as real.

variants.headline: From abroad: {{first}} and {{second}} stand together
body: Letters from foreign courts relate that {{first}} and {{second}} have concluded a defensive pact. The news reached us by way of travelers and is here set down as it came.

variants.headline: {{first}} and {{second}} end their defensive pact
body: The defensive pact between {{first}} and {{second}} has ended. The two states are not at war with each other, and the split appears to be a matter of policy rather than arms.

variants.headline: A foreign pact falls away
body: A defensive pact between two foreign powers has ended. The two states are not at war with each other, and the change came quietly.

variants.headline: What the end of the {{first}} and {{second}} pact leaves open
body: The pact that once made {{first}} and {{second}} a single problem now makes them two. Alliances that end without a war leave open ground between the former partners, and open ground is where third parties try their luck.

variants.headline: The fence between two gardens
body: Two neighbors took down their shared fence. The gardens still grow, and the fox is listening.

variants.headline: We declare friendship with {{friend}}
body: Our nation and {{friend}} have declared friendship. The two states have set aside hostility and pledged their goodwill publicly.

variants.headline: A friendship declared
body: Our nation has declared friendship with a major power. Hostility between the two states has been set aside in favor of public goodwill.

variants.headline: Hear it! Friendship with {{friend}}
body: Good news for every hearth. Our nation and {{friend}} have declared friendship, and the word is official. Pass it on.

variants.headline: Sir, a good word travels slowly
body: Your readers may note that friendship with {{friend}} is declared, and I write to say the news is welcome in our house as well. Two peoples who trade and talk rarely find reason to draw blades. May this friendship pay its way in quiet years.

variants.headline: The tavern drank to {{friend}} last night
body: When the crier called the news, the room raised its cups to {{friend}} without being asked. Foreign policy is a long way from this street, but a friendly flag is good for business.

variants.headline: Our friendship with {{friend}} is over
body: The declaration of friendship between our nation and {{friend}} has come to an end. The public goodwill it pledged is withdrawn, and relations between the two states return to plainer terms.

variants.headline: A friendship ends
body: A declaration of friendship between our nation and a major power has come to an end. The public goodwill it pledged is withdrawn.

variants.headline: In memoriam: the friendship with {{friend}}
body: It began with toasted words and open markets, and for a time our two flags made a pleasant pair on the river. The declaration is ended now, and the friendship with it. What remains is the memory that such a thing was possible.

variants.headline: The end of the {{friend}} friendship, weighed
body: Friendship declarations carry no armies, but they carry credit, and credit is what the court of {{friend}} has now withdrawn. What follows is usually a cooler exchange of envoys rather than a hotter exchange of arrows. The record does not yet say which this will be.

variants.headline: {{vassal}} becomes our vassal
body: {{vassal}} has entered vassalage under our nation. Their court now answers to ours in the conduct of their state.

variants.headline: In this year, {{vassal}} was made subject
body: In this season the realm was enlarged, and {{vassal}} was recorded among its subjects. The court received the envoys of the new vassal and set its name in the rolls.

variants.headline: What {{vassal}} adds to our standing
body: A vassal is land, tribute and a buffer, all at once, and {{vassal}} brings all three. The cost is the defending of it: their enemies are now ours to watch. On balance the paper calls it a gain, and the map agrees.

variants.headline: Order, properly extended
body: The union with {{vassal}} will be called many things in many taverns. The paper's view is plain: a strong hand at the center is what keeps the peace, and the realm now has one more province under its steady guidance.

variants.headline: {{vassal}} is no longer our vassal
body: The vassalage binding {{vassal}} to our nation has ended. The two states no longer stand in the relation of master and subject.

variants.headline: One vassalage ends
body: A vassalage binding another state to our nation has ended. The two parties no longer stand in the relation of master and subject.

variants.headline: {{vassal}} walks free of us
body: Where we once commanded, we now negotiate. {{vassal}} out of our orbit is a border to watch and a precedent for every other vassal who heard the news. The strong keep what they can hold; the paper leaves the rest unsaid.

variants.headline: Our mastery of {{vassal}}, concluded
body: It held while it held: tribute, garrisons and the quiet pride of a subject province. The vassalage of {{vassal}} is dissolved, and what survives of the old arrangement is the memory of it.

variants.headline: We and {{civilization}} denounce each other
body: Denunciations now run both ways between our nation and {{civilization}}. Each court has publicly condemned the other, and the exchange is on the record in both directions.

variants.headline: Both courts speak, and neither yields
body: Our denunciation of {{civilization}} has been answered in kind, and the exchange is now official in both directions. There is no ambiguity left to trade on: the two states are adversaries on the record.

variants.headline: Two houses, one quarrel
body: When both neighbors shout at once, the market counts the broken pots. Quiet houses keep full shelves.

variants.headline: Who pays for the shouting?
body: The court traded denunciations with {{civilization}} this season, and the language was fine on both sides. What the court has not said is what the quarrel costs the people who pay for it. The paper asks for the price before it applauds the pride.

variants.headline: We open our borders to {{civilization}}
body: Our nation has granted open borders to {{civilization}}. Their travelers and caravans may now cross our land without leave for each journey.

variants.headline: Our borders stand open to a neighbor
body: Our nation has granted open borders to a neighboring power. Their travelers and caravans may now cross our land without leave for each journey.

variants.headline: Notice to merchants: our roads are open to {{civilization}}
body: Take note, traders and caravan masters. The borders of our nation stand open to {{civilization}}, and their goods and travelers may cross our land freely. The frontier posts are instructed accordingly.

variants.headline: Open borders with {{civilization}}, and the goodwill they carry
body: An open border is a small treaty renewed every day by the people who use it. {{civilization}}'s caravans on our roads mean traffic at our markets and a neighbor with something to lose from trouble. The paper counts that a bargain in our favor.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} opens its borders to us
body: {{civilization}} has granted us open borders. Our travelers and caravans may now cross their land without leave for each journey.

variants.headline: A neighbor opens its borders to us
body: A neighboring power has granted us open borders. Our travelers and caravans may now cross their land without leave for each journey.

variants.headline: The road to {{capital}} is open
body: {{civilization}} has opened its borders to us, and our caravans can now reach {{capital}} without a permit at the frontier. Merchants who have watched that road for seasons are already loading carts.

variants.headline: Bart the carter is first through the gate
body: When word came down that {{civilization}} had opened the border, Bart had his wagon loaded by noon. "Stared at that road my whole life," he says. "First time it has gone somewhere."

variants.headline: {{from}} and {{to}} deal for peace
body: A deal struck between {{from}} and {{to}} includes an end to war with a third party. One of the two signatories has agreed, in the bargain, to make peace with a state that is not at the table.

variants.headline: Peace is part of the price
body: A deal between two states has been recorded, and part of its price is peace: one of the parties has agreed, in the bargain, to end a war with a third party.

variants.when: from !== null && to !== null && fromGives !== null && toGives !== null
variants.headline: The terms, as recorded
body: {{from}} gives: {{fromGives}}.
{{to}} gives: {{toGives}}.
Among it all, peace with a third party, bought and signed.

variants.when: from !== null && to !== null && ours === false
variants.headline: A war ends at a negotiating table
body: The deal between {{from}} and {{to}} settles a war at a table at least one seat away from the fighting. Peace bought this way tends to last exactly as long as the payment. Watch which borders go quiet, and for how long.

variants.headline: War is written into the deal between {{from}} and {{to}}
body: A deal between {{from}} and {{to}} includes an agreement to make war on a third party. Somewhere beyond the two signatories, someone is about to learn what their bargain costs.

variants.headline: A deal with war in the terms
body: A deal between two states has been recorded with war in its terms: one party has agreed to take up arms against a third.

variants.when: from !== null && to !== null && ours === false
variants.headline: Tonight: a deal that buys a war
body: From the foreign desk: {{from}} and {{to}} have signed a deal, and part of it is war against a third power. No shots reported yet. We will follow this story.

variants.when: from !== null && to !== null && ours === false
variants.headline: Other people's wars, other people's coin
body: The deal between {{from}} and {{to}} puts a third nation's name on a contract that nation never signed. The paper's question is for our own court: when that war reaches a border we care about, what did we do while the ink dried?

variants.headline: Our vassalage to {{master}} is over
body: The vassalage that bound our nation to {{master}} has ended. Our state no longer answers to their court, and stands again on its own authority.

variants.headline: We are no longer a vassal
body: The vassalage that bound our nation to a foreign power has ended. Our state stands again on its own authority.

variants.headline: Hear it! We bow no more
body: People of the nation, the word is official. The vassalage to {{master}} is ended, and our court answers to no throne but our own. Say it in the square, and say it twice.

variants.headline: In this year, the vassalage was dissolved
body: In this season the record shows the vassalage to {{master}} dissolved, and the tribute that traveled with it carried no more. The old arrangement of tribute and protection is ended; what follows is not yet written.

variants.headline: Free, and with work to do
body: No one in the square needs telling what the end of the {{master}} vassalage means. But freedom is a running expense, not a festival. The paper asks the court for arms, allies and grain stores, in that order, before the old master's mood changes.

variants.headline: We denounce {{civilization}}
body: Our nation has publicly denounced {{civilization}}. The declaration puts our hostility toward their court on the record, short of open war.

variants.headline: Said plainly, and none too soon
body: The denunciation of {{civilization}} is on the record, and the paper approves of plain speaking over patient smiling. Words do not stop armies, but they tell our allies whose side we are on while there is still time to matter.

variants.byline: A reader who trades across that border
variants.headline: Sir, was there no quieter road?
body: I read that our court has denounced {{civilization}}, and I think of the carts that cross that border in both directions. Quarrels are cheap to declare and dear to keep. If a word can be taken back with honor, I ask the court whether it should be.

variants.headline: In this year, we spoke against {{civilization}}
body: In this season the court set down a denunciation against {{civilization}}, where none stood before. The record notes the fact and the date, and leaves the judgment to others.
